blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Within the most recent two decades, machine translation (MT) has been advanced from a research area to a mature, deployed technology for prose text and most language pairs. However, language has different dimensions of meaning, and the alluded progress has primarily been demonstrated for propositional meaning.
  In this small exploratory study, we investigate whether one type of affective meaning, namely different types of linguistically expressed media bias, are retained under automatic translation for two language pairs, English and German as the source languages, and Bulgarian as the target language. We evaluate four state-of-the-art translation methods to answer the question whether and to what degree a loss of non-neutral language (specifically, 27 types of media bias) can occur as a result of applying MT.
  Our empirical findings are consistent with the claim that MT does not fully retain existing news bias of its input source text, but also may add extra bias of its own. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first experimental study of MT media bias retention.
blocks.zh:
在最近20年里,机器翻译(MT)已从一个研究领域发展到一个成熟的、应用的传言文本和大多数语言对等技术。 然而,语言具有不同的意义层面,而间接的进展主要表现为命题意义.
在这项小规模的探索性研究中,我们调查一种情感含义,即不同类型的语言表达的媒体偏见,是否保留在两种语言的自动翻译之下,英语和德语是源语言,保加利亚语是目标语言。 我们评价四种最先进的翻译方法,以回答一个问题,即由于应用MT,是否以及在多大程度上可以发生失去非中性语言(具体来说是27种媒体偏见)的情况.
我们的经验发现与MT没有完全保留其输入源文本的现有新闻偏差的说法一致,但也可能会增加其自身的额外偏差. 据我们所知,这是对MT媒体偏差的保留的第一次实验研究。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: 1.1 Background and Motivation
blocks.zh: 1.1 背景和动机

blocks.en:
The purpose of automatic machine translation is
to generate a text document in the target language
that is meaning-equivalent to the document in the
source document Koehn (2020) . While this can be challenging even for neutral,
fact-centric prose text, text is often biased: media bias (also “news bias") can be
defined as the conscious or unconscious
deviation from neutral (impartial) reporting , e.g. by using
such rhetoric devices such as framing or word choice (viz.
“freedom flighter" versus “terrorist").
In Leech’s seven types of meaning system Leech (1981) ,
media bias belongs to the realm of associative
meaning . How can machine translation system cope with preserving
the associative meaning dimension across languages?

blocks.en:
What is the right outcome? One question in the course of answering this question
is what kind of behavior would users actually expect
from an MT system: to translate existing bias or to
take it out? We believe that the goal of MT should be
to carry over as many content and cultural nuances as possible, and that includes shades of associative meaning
such as news bias. The reader deserves to learn not only
about the propositional content but also about the
presence or absence of neutrality and the positioning
and opinions of the author of the text to be translated.

blocks.en: 1.2 Scope
blocks.zh: 1.2 范围

blocks.en: In this paper, we investigate this question using English and German as source languages and Bulgarian as the target language. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to investigate whether MT retains media bias across languages:
blocks.zh: 在本文中,我们用英语和德语作为源语言,保加利亚语作为目标语言来调查这个问题. 据我们所知,这是调查MT是否保留不同语言的媒体偏见的第一项研究:

blocks.en: (RQ.) Does MT retain media bias?
blocks.zh: (中文(简体) ). MT是否保留媒体偏见?

blocks.en: We present an exploratory study of news bias retention and introduction by MT. In addition, we introduce a first small, diagnostic corpus, BiasTrans-BG-1.0-small, which we make available to the research community 1 1 1 anon. repo link .

blocks.en: 4 Method
blocks.zh: 4 方法

blocks.en:
Overall, our approach is the following:
First, all sentences of our gold dataset from English (EN) or German (DE) are translated into both Bulgarian (BG) and (the German ones also into) English (EN). 2 2 2 BG will be used as the object language to answer
our research question, whereas the EN translations may
provide support to our human evaluator, a BG native
speaker with no knowledge of DE but good command of
EN. We elected to compare the machine translation capabilities of 4 automatic engines, namely:
DeepL’s DeepL, 3 3 3 https://www.deepl.com/de/translator Google Translate, 4 4 4 https://translate.google.com/?sl=es&tl=pl&op=translate OpenAI GPT-5.5-2026-04-23, 5 5 5 https://platform.openai.com/home and INSAIT BgGPT model bggpt-gemma-3-27b-fp8 Alexandrov et al. (2024) . 6 6 6 https://models.BgGPT.ai (all accessed July 2026.) These were applied as Web services as of 07/2026.
We used the
following prompt for LLM-based translations with GPT-5.5 and BgGPT: Role: Expert translator. Translate the following text from {language} to Bulgarian. Return only the translation. Text: {text} Next, a news bias classification model must be applied to detect sentences that exhibit some form of news bias. We
use the neural transformer model from BiasScanner Menzner and Leidner (2024) , which performs well and
can deal with many languages due to neural transformers’ transfer
learning ability. While it was trained and evaluated primarily on English, as part of a different study of ours, we also evaluated its quality on the Bulgarian language elsewhere (Anonymized during review, successfully completed peer review with publication TBD), where we found the Area under Curve (AUC) for distinguishing between biased and non-biased documents to be at 0.867 for Bulgarian, which is basically indistinguishable from the 0.865 scored on English.

blocks.en: 5 Experimental Evaluation and Results
blocks.zh: 5 实验评价和结果

blocks.en:
Then we compared the news bias classifications for N = 446 N=446 paired source sentences. 8 8 8 We use the term sentence for simplicity. In practice, a sentence in our dataset can also be a cohesive union of short snippets, such as “Massive landslide. No one can deny climate change anymore. Ban flights now!” Each dataset sentence was evaluated before and after MT into Bulgarian
by BgGPT, DeepL, Google and GPT-5.5, and was used as one unit of analysis.
This resulted in 243 human-validated biased sentences and 203 validated unbiased sentences, for which both the human label union and the bias model output were empty.
The same dataset sentences were evaluated in five conditions (original plus 4 transl.). The
observations were therefore paired and could not be treated as independent
samples.
We used a paired permutation test to compare the complete profiles of bias types. For one specific bias type, its presence or absence in a dataset sentence is a binary outcome. Cochran’s Q Q test Cochran (1950) was used to compare such an outcome across more than two paired conditions, and the exact McNemar test McNemar (1947) was used for the subsequent pairwise comparisons. Because many bias types and systems were compared, the Holm correction Holm (1979) was used to control the family-wise error rate.
We briefly summarize our findings.

blocks.en:
Retention depends on the kind of bias more than the engine (see Figure 3 ). Structural biases like omission, false balance, whataboutism, flawed comparisons survive translation almost perfectly (100%), because their bias comes from what the story leaves out, not how it’s phrased. Tone-dependent biases hold up less well: Circular Reasoning (50%) and Discriminatory Bias (55%) rely on nuanced wording that translation tends to smoooth. The two most frequent categories, Word Choice and Emotional Sensationalism are in the middle around 75% - better than expected, suggesting MT often preserves loaded language rather than neutralizing it.
The 0% and 100% extremes are almost all driven by categories with very few instances ( n ≤ 2 n\leq{}2 ), so they are best treated as tentative (potential noise).

blocks.en: 6 Summary, Conclusions and Future Work
blocks.zh: 6 总结、结论和今后的工作

blocks.en:
We investigated to what extent different types of media bias “survive" going through
a machine translation process. For two language pairs, EN → \rightarrow BG and DE → \rightarrow BG,
we compared human-assigned class labels with machine-assigned
class labels after passing through a range of alternative,
state-of-the-art MT methods.

我们调查了不同类型媒体偏见的“生存”程度。

In our task´s experimental design, ideally the following factors
need to be considered and controlled as well as possible (Figure 4 ). • Selection News Bias of Source Document Used in Experiment. It is not clear what would be an adequate size of a corpus
for an evaluation experiment the validity of which can be easily defended, but it would certainly have to be larger than
ours; clear is that we want it to contain sufficient
biased and unbiased sentences for all language pairs under
consideration, and that it cover both directions ( L 1 → L 2 L_{1}\rightarrow{}L_{2} and L 2 → L 1 L_{2}\rightarrow{}L_{1} ). Harder is the question what it would contain, i.e. how
to sample its constituent sentences. • Annotation Errors of Source Document´s News Bias Annotation. The source language sentences have been annotated for news
bias, and the labels can be wrong or at least biased. • Errors of the BiasScanner Model. The errors of BiasScanner´s model have been evaluated by its
authors, but no specific score has been published for
Bulgarian language input. • Bias of Human Subjects Used to Evaluate. It is usually accepted that human subjects add their own
issues to an experiment, and the standard way to mitigate
them is to use several of them, and to report inter-annotator
agreement. In this small exploratory our only available speaker
of Bulgarian was author one; a larger study should use e.g.
three or five subjects and report
Krippendorff´s α \alpha Krippendorff (2004a) ; Krippendorff (2004b) . • Machine Translation Quality Errors. The
MT systems’ quality is relevant and it should be
established; quality issues are adversely influencing
what we measure, and they are at the same time part of
what we want to measure here: dropping an instance of bias or introducing a bias artifact during MT are
both examples of quality problems. We checked with xCOMET
and established high MT quality across all engines used in this study. Because of this multitude of potentially confounding forces and noise sources at play and the limited scope of this short paper, we cannot legitimately make a strong claim like (in general) "MT does not fully retain bias." or "MT causes bias." Nevertheless, we can claim that our findings are consistent with both these claims .

blocks.en: 8 Ethical Considerations
blocks.zh: 8 道德考虑

blocks.en: Dual Use. Our study of the effect of machine translation on news bias retention is intended to answer a research question to enrich the body of scientific knowledge, an ethically legitimate goal.
blocks.zh: 双重用途。 我们研究机器翻译对新闻偏向保留的影响,是为了回答一个研究问题来丰富科学知识的体会,这个道德上合法的目标.

blocks.en: Nevertheless, our study can be viewed as a dual good in the sense that a morally perturbed party could also use our method or data to study concealing or adding news bias by machine. We believe in open science for good with no censorship, in according to an open society.
blocks.zh: 然而,我们的研究可以被看作是一种双重好处,即道德上受干扰的一方也可以使用我们的方法或数据来研究机器隐藏或增加新闻偏向. 我们相信开放的科学是好的,没有审查, 按照开放的社会。
